t: The Oyo Empire was a Yoruba savannah state whose cavalry made it the leading power between the Niger and the Volta.
It grew rich on tribute and the Atlantic slave trade, forcing Dahomey into vassalage and shaping the Bight of Benin coast.
Feuds between king and chiefs, Afonja's revolt and the Ilorin emirate destroyed it; Oyo-Ile was abandoned c. 1835–1836.
dyk: Oyo's council of chiefs could reject an Alaafin by presenting him with an empty calabash or parrots' eggs, after which the king was expected to take his own life.
ev: Alaafin Abipa reoccupies Oyo-Ile after some eighty years of exile
Oyo begins repeated cavalry invasions of Dahomey
A treaty confirms Dahomey as a tribute-paying vassal of Oyo
Alaafin Abiodun overthrows and executes Basorun Gaa, who had dominated the state
Alaafin Awole is forced to take his own life after his war chiefs mutiny
Afonja rebels at Ilorin with Fulani and Hausa support inspired by the Sokoto jihad
Oyo-Ile is abandoned; Alaafin Atiba founds a reduced state at New Oyo
New Oyo signs a treaty with the British
